Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run Rust project** that

1. Reads the current clipboard text (Windows, macOS, Linux).
2. Sends that text to the ElevenLabs TTS API.
3. Streams the returned MP3/OGG audio to your speakers.

> **TL;DR**  
> ```bash
> cargo run --release
> ```

---

## 1. Project layout

```
elevenlabs-tts-clipboard/
├─ Cargo.toml
└─ src/
   └─ main.rs
```

---

## 2. `Cargo.toml`

```toml
[package]
name = "elevenlabs-tts-clipboard"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
# Clipboard access
clipboard = "0.7"

# HTTP client
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }

# Async runtime
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

# JSON (de)serialization
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

# Audio playback
rodio = "0.17"

# Error handling
anyhow = "1"

# Environment variable handling
dotenvy = "0.15"
```

> **Why these crates?**  
> * `clipboard` – cross‑platform clipboard access.  
> * `reqwest` – async HTTP client with streaming support.  
> * `tokio` – async runtime required by `reqwest`.  
> * `rodio` – simple audio playback (supports MP3/OGG).  
> * `anyhow` – ergonomic error handling.  
> * `dotenvy` – load `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` from a `.env` file (optional).
